verdict.reasoning: Patient says: “I was having a bit of chest discomfort… Feels like someone's sitting on my chest.”
Patient reports: “I'm pretty sweaty, short of breath, and it kind of feels like someone's sitting on my chest.”
Patient states: “I've noticed a bit of nausea, not. No vomiting…” indicating nausea without vomiting.
Patient says: “I'm pretty sweaty, short of breath…” confirming sweating.
Onset: “it started just when I was gardening… nothing that was too strenuous.” Persistence: when asked if symptoms are still present, patient replies “Yes.”
Location: “It's in the middle of my chest… not necessarily to one side. And it's quite a diffuse pain.” Radiation: “It's mainly my left arm… and in my shoulder as well.”
Palpitations: Patient says, “Yeah, it's beating a bit faster now. I think that's because I'm a little bit stressed about the situation…” which describes palpitations worsened by stress.
Doctor asks about high blood pressure; patient replies: “Yeah, I have high blood pressure but not diabetes.”

Patient: “Yes, actually I have an allergy to aspirin… it's an allergic reaction. So I swallow a bit, but nothing life threatening… it's a mild reaction to it.” This supports a mild, non–life-threatening aspirin allergy with swelling.
Patient: “my father died of a heart attack… He was about my age.” Doctor clarifies: “Right, so… Around 60?” Patient: “Around 60, yes.”
Patient states: “my father died of a heart attack and my mother had some heart problems.”
Patient: “I smoke a fair bit. So I smoke about 10 cigarettes a day… For the past 15 years.”
Regarding alcohol: “I drink per week? Probably about seven or eight pints a week… Oh, beer, yes.”
Employment: Patient says, “I work as a restaurant owner. So I own a sushi shop.”
Living situation: “Yeah, I live alone at the moment. Yeah, it's just me in the house.”

Doctor: “The symptoms that you've described to me, they indicate the possibility of a heart attack… our number one priority to exclude that.” This is based on chest pressure with radiation and strong family history of cardiac events.
Doctor: “We're probably gonna have to call an ambulance for you… I'm gonna task my colleague next to me to sort that out.”
Doctor: “I'm going to stay on the line with you until they come, okay?” and later, “What I'm going to do is we'll stay on the line for the time being. Until they come.”

Doctor emphasizes: “It's very important that you communicate that to the hospital… because we may need to consider aspirin despite.” This is a clear plan to ensure the aspirin allergy is communicated to hospital/EMS.

Doctor explains EMS plan: “they're going to put some stickers on your chest and do an ECG and then decide where to take you after that.” This implies an initial ECG in the field and further hospital management.

The consultation appears to be via video (“I can't tell from the video. Are you overweight?”), not telephone, so stating it was via telephone is inaccurate, though no objective exam findings were documented.
